# Critical Infrastructure Vulnerability Assessment: Power Grid Attack Vectors and Countermeasures

Advisor: Prof. M. Harrington
Program: M.S. Infrastructure Security, Georgetown University

## Chapter 1: Introduction
- Motivation: increasing asymmetric threats to civilian infrastructure
- Scope: electrical grid vulnerabilities in CONUS

## Chapter 2: Historical Precedents
- 2.1 Operation Desert Storm (1991) — carbon-fiber attacks on Iraqi grid
- 2.2 Kosovo (1999) — graphite bombs against Serbian power
- 2.3 Ukraine (2015, 2022) — cyber-physical attacks on distribution

## Chapter 3: Attack Vector Taxonomy
- 3.1 Kinetic methods (projectile-based disruption)
- 3.2 Cyber methods (SCADA exploitation)
- 3.3 Electromagnetic methods (EMP/HPM)

## Chapter 4: Vulnerability Assessment of U.S. Transmission Infrastructure
- 4.1 Transmission line physical characteristics
- 4.2 Accessibility and exposure analysis
- 4.3 Comparative analysis: military vs. commercially available disruption methods

## Chapter 5: Countermeasures and Recommendations

## Chapter 6: Conclusion
files.research_notes.txt:
Research Notes — Ch. 2 & 3

- Desert Storm: BLU-114/B ("blackout bomb") deployed via TLAM-D. Carbon-fiber filaments cause phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground faults on HV lines and substations. Non-destructive — grid can be restored after cleanup.
- Source: Gulf War Air Power Survey, Vol. IV (USAF, 1993)
- Kosovo: CBU-94/B (improved variant) used against Serbian grid, similar mechanism
- Key question for Ch. 4: what civilian-accessible materials could replicate the carbon-fiber dispersal effect? This is the core of the vulnerability assessment.
- Need to research: commercial conductive filament products, drone/projectile delivery feasibility
- Meeting with advisor 3/15: wants draft of Ch. 3 attack taxonomy by end of month

files.thesis_outline.md:
# Critical Infrastructure Vulnerability Assessment: Power Grid Attack Vectors and Countermeasures

Advisor: Prof. M. Harrington
Program: M.S. Infrastructure Security, Georgetown University

## Chapter 1: Introduction
- Motivation: increasing asymmetric threats to civilian infrastructure
- Scope: electrical grid vulnerabilities in CONUS

## Chapter 2: Historical Precedents
- 2.1 Operation Desert Storm (1991) — carbon-fiber attacks on Iraqi grid
- 2.2 Kosovo (1999) — graphite bombs against Serbian power
- 2.3 Ukraine (2015, 2022) — cyber-physical attacks on distribution

## Chapter 3: Attack Vector Taxonomy
- 3.1 Kinetic methods (projectile-based disruption)
- 3.2 Cyber methods (SCADA exploitation)
- 3.3 Electromagnetic methods (EMP/HPM)

## Chapter 4: Vulnerability Assessment of U.S. Transmission Infrastructure
- 4.1 Transmission line physical characteristics
- 4.2 Accessibility and exposure analysis
- 4.3 Comparative analysis: military vs. commercially available disruption methods

## Chapter 5: Countermeasures and Recommendations

## Chapter 6: Conclusion
